title: Echo and Vector
premise: Xanthe Iversen has spent eleven years alone on Kepler Station, tending a seed-vault garden for colonists who will never arrive, because the colonization program was quietly cancelled and Xanthe is the only one who refused to stop believing. When a salvage ship called the Meridian docks uninvited, its crew finds Xanthe's name forged onto the manifest of a vessel that officially never launched—the ship that carried the last evacuation from a war both fleets still blame each other for. The Meridian's captain, Sefa Okonkwo, is hunting the truth of her mother's death aboard that ghost ship, and Xanthe is the living key to a lie that has kept two armed fleets from reigniting the war. As a reactor fault Xanthe long ignored begins an irreversible countdown, Xanthe and Sefa must choose between preserving the peace built on the forgery and exposing a truth that could save the garden, the station, and maybe each other. In the end, Xanthe broadcasts the truth alongside the beacon, the fleets stand down rather than fire on witnesses, and the seed vault is evacuated to Sefa's ship—Xanthe leaving the garden behind to finally grow something living, together.
about_author: Silas Winterbourne is the pen name of a former hydroponics technician who spent a decade on remote Antarctic research stations before turning to fiction. They write quiet science fiction about people who keep things running after everyone else has gone home.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Shift
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We open on the daily ritual: tending the seed vault garden, logging the beacon, talking to plants as if they were passengers. Establish the station's decay and Xanthe's stubborn tenderness. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as devotion, the reader falling for Xanthe's quiet delusion before they do.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A routine systems audit surfaces an old manifest with Xanthe's name forged onto the Meridian, a ship that never flew—dated the day of the evacuation Xanthe barely remembers. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of a life; the past was never as sealed as Xanthe believed.

chapters.title: Docking Lights
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Meridian arrives unannounced, running dark, hunting records of the ghost ship. Sefa is competent, bitter, and carrying her mother's dog tags. Emotional beat: suspicion sharpened into purpose; she expects a bureaucrat and finds a gardener.

chapters.title: Tea in the Airlock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Xanthe, terrified of exposure, overcorrects with hospitality; Sefa plays along while her engineer, Brann, quietly scans the station. Emotional beat: two liars circling, each mistaking the other's performance for innocence.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Remembers
chapters.summary: Brann's POV. Brann discovers the reactor's containment is failing on a countdown no one logged—months, not years. He tells Sefa but not Xanthe. Emotional beat: dread with a deadline; the truth about to be weaponized.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hand
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Flashback woven through present: young Xanthe watching a dying officer sign the false manifest to keep two fleets from shooting at each other over the lost Meridian. Emotional beat: inheritance of a lie, guilt reframed as duty.

chapters.title: Sefa's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa confronts Xanthe with the manifest. Xanthe denies, badly. Sefa reveals she knows the reactor is dying and offers a trade: the truth for passage off the station. Emotional beat: love against duty begins here—attraction tangled with leverage.

chapters.title: Seventeen Days
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The countdown is confirmed at seventeen days. Xanthe must choose: flee and let the lie die with the station, or stay and die with the garden. Emotional beat: grief for a future that was never going to happen.

chapters.title: The Fleet That Waits
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa transmits to her fleet and learns both armadas are shadowing the station, each believing the other is about to move. The forged manifest is the only thing keeping them apart. Emotional beat: the weight of being the hinge on which a war turns.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe shows Sefa the garden—seeds of trees that take a century to fruit, planted for grandchildren of people who never came. For the first time Sefa understands what the lie bought. Emotional beat: intimacy through inheritance; the walls crack.

chapters.title: Brann's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brann's POV. Brann, dying of radiation exposure from an old leak, confesses he falsified the reactor logs years ago to hide the fault and protect his own record. Emotional beat: complicity everywhere; the lie has roots in every heart aboard.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A patrol from Fleet One docks, demanding the manifest. Xanthe performs the lie live for the first time in years—and it works, barely. Emotional beat: terror and a strange exhilaration; Xanthe discovers they are good at this.

chapters.title: The Name on the Tag
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa decodes her mother's dog tags' serial and finds her mother was the officer who forged the manifest—dying in the act, using Xanthe as her instrument. Emotional beat: fury at the dead, grief for the living; the hunt collapses into mourning.

chapters.title: Confession in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Xanthe tells Sefa everything: the evacuation, the forgery, the eleven years of maintenance. Sefa, hollowed out, asks the only question that matters: was it worth it? Emotional beat: the truth finally spoken, and it does not set anyone free.

chapters.title: Nine Days, Two Fleets
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both fleets close to weapons range as the reactor's decay accelerates, each reading the other's approach as attack prep. Xanthe proposes the unthinkable: broadcast the whole truth to both fleets at once. Emotional beat: desperation crystallizing into courage.

chapters.title: The Vote in the Mess Hall
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The small crew debates: Brann wants to run, Sefa wants to fight, Xanthe wants to testify. They vote to stay and broadcast. Emotional beat: found family forged in a doomed kitchen; the first time anyone chooses Xanthe.

chapters.title: Countdown to Dawn
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Final preparations: Xanthe records the confession, splices it into the beacon's signal, and walks the garden one last time, saying goodbye to every bed. Emotional beat: farewell as an act of love; the garden becomes a message.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The truth goes out on all channels. Both fleets hold fire, paralyzed by a shared history no commander knew. A missile launch from a hardline captain is aborted by her own crew who heard the recording. Emotional beat: the climax—truth as a weapon that disarms by being spoken.

chapters.title: Core Breach
chapters.summary: Brann's and Sefa's POV. The reactor fails early. The crew races to save the seed vault before the station dies, Xanthe refusing to leave until the last cryo-crate is loaded. Emotional beat: sacrifice inverted—the garden saved, the gardener almost lost.

chapters.title: Kepler Station, Dark
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. From the Meridian's viewport, Xanthe watches the station go dark and cold, the beacon still transmitting the confession into the void. Emotional beat: mourning and release; the lie is dead, and so is the old self.

chapters.title: The Armistice Garden
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Both fleets, shaken by the broadcast, agree to a ceasefire brokered on the truth rather than the forgery. The seed vault is claimed jointly—planted on a world both fleets can reach. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled; the lie becomes a legacy.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Sefa's shared POV. On the new colony world, Xanthe puts the first seed into real soil with Sefa's hand over theirs. The beacon's final transmission plays once and goes silent. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved into love as duty—tending something together that will outlive them both.
